checkpoint_review: The Router's verdicts are largely accurate. It correctly identified that hindquarters, hooves, and tail are untestable due to cropping/occlusion. For the testable checkpoints (Head, Face, Shoulder Hump, Fur), the 'is_present: true' judgments are supported by visual evidence. The Router was not too lenient; the visible features strongly match the bison taxonomy.
artifact_review: The Router identified texture anomalies (fur edges) and blur (grass). The Perceptual Quality Auditor added 'slight compression' (0.2 severity). The Topology Boundary Auditor found a high-confidence mask (0.98), suggesting the main body is structurally coherent, though the mask image shows some fragmentation at the very bottom right (likely noise or separate object). The Animal Pose Auditor flagged low confidence in hind limbs, but this aligns with the Router's 'untestable' verdict for that region due to occlusion/grass. I agree with the Router's severity assessments; the artifacts are minor and typical of AI generation (soft edges, painted background) rather than catastrophic structural failures.
alignment_reasoning: The fine-grained classifier confirmed 'bison' with high confidence (logit 7.87). All visible anatomical checkpoints (head, horn, beard, hump, fur) are present and correct. The image conforms well to the class definition despite partial occlusion.
artifact_reasoning: Minor texture anomalies at fur-background boundaries and slight 'painted' look to foreground grass. No structural melting or fusion detected in the visible forequarters. Low pose confidence in hind legs is explained by occlusion, not necessarily artifact. Overall quality is good but lacks the crispness of a high-end photograph.
